first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest: 63.37m shares, 31.5% of float, 2.5 days to cover on 2026-05-15 (MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HIMS/short-interest/); 61.2m, about 26% of float, 3.2 days on 2026-07-10 (Equibles https://equibles.com/stocks/hims/shortinterest); 58.7m, 4.5 days on 2026-08-14 (Curved Trading, snippet only, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/hims/short-interest/). Six of the last seven reactions were negative (median abs 12.36%).

evidence.text: WW International's Q3 2026 release (5 Nov) shows clinical (GLP-1 telehealth) subscribers falling from 197k at the start of Q3 to 174k at the end, a net loss of about 23k (-12% q/q), though still +40% y/y. This is a peer read that telehealth GLP-1 retention or acquisition weakened in Q3 2026, the quarter HIMS reports. HIMS's own Q2 subscribers were 2.891m, and weight loss is its largest growth driver.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscriber and weight-loss lines drove the Q1 2026 (-14.1%) and Q2 2025 (-12.36%) reactions per the baseline. Q2 2026 subscribers +19% y/y with a revenue beat still saw -3.97%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Released four days ago by a small-cap peer. HIMS previews do not cite it, and the HIMS consensus revenue ($893m) still sits in the upper half of the guide. If the market had transmitted this, the revenue bar would have drifted toward the bottom of the guide. A -24% 20-day run-up may already partly reflect sector worry.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. WW is a different business model (behavioural plus clinical) and much smaller. HIMS has not confirmed this. Novo's Q3 data (separate finding) points the other way on branded-channel volume.

evidence.text: Novo Nordisk's Q3 2026 6-K (4 Nov) reports about 3.6m US Wegovy pill prescriptions in Q3 (more than 8m since the 5 Jan launch) and combined US Wegovy +21% at CER in Q3. About 35% of 4.1m injectable Wegovy prescriptions went through the self-pay channel, which includes telehealth; HIMS sells these under its March 2026 Novo agreement. Novo also cites lower realised prices.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Branded GLP-1 mix is the stated driver of the gross-margin compression that sold the Q2 2026 print (-3.97%) despite revenue $753m vs about $695m expected. More branded volume helps revenue but has hurt the margin line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Counterparty data released after HIMS last spoke (10 Aug). Novo does not name HIMS, so desks may not map it to HIMS. If it were priced, HIMS would not have fallen about 20% since 22 Oct while its main supplier's US self-pay volume grew.
evidence.independence: Direct counterparty, but transmission to HIMS is not confirmed: Novo refers only to 'multiple telehealth organisations'. It conflicts with the WW peer data above. Lower realised prices cut against HIMS revenue per subscriber.

evidence.text: The full-year guide needs a large Q4 EBITDA step-up. FY26 adj. EBITDA guide $275-325m, minus H1 actuals ($44.3m Q1 + $60.3m Q2 = $104.6m), minus the Q3 guide midpoint ($85m), implies Q4 adj. EBITDA of about $85-135m. That is a 9-13% margin against 8% in Q2. Gross margin fell from 76% to 64% y/y, and management said it will stay below historical levels through H2. The FY EBITDA top end has already been cut twice in 2026 ($350m to $325m in Aug). A third trim, or a Q4 implied below the street, is the line this stock has traded on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: EBITDA and margin miss plus weak outlook, -14.1%. Q2 2026: EPS miss and gross margin down with FY EBITDA top end cut, -3.97%. Q4 2024 (Feb 2025): guide, -22.32%. Q2 2025: -12.36%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but no preview found states the implied Q4 EBITDA. The street focuses on Q3 revenue of about $893m. Against that, the -24% 20-day run-up and the stock trading 43% below its 52-week high suggest some of this is priced. If it were fully priced, call skew would not be bid over puts.
evidence.independence: Q1 and Q1/Q2 release figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000074/hims-20260331x8xkearningsr.htm). Management's 'meaningful step-up in adjusted EBITDA dollars in the second half' (Q2 call, https://www.webull.com/news/15420770610291712) argues the step-up is planned, which is why this is small and not large.

evidence.text: Q3 cash flow is a test of a stated promise. Q2 operating cash flow was -$35.9m and FCF -$68.2m, driven by receivables rising from $32.1m to $375.3m. Of that, $347.4m is manufacturer discount and rebate receivables under vendor supply agreements, per the Q2 10-Q. Management said it expects to 'resume free cash flow generation in the second half' and set up a $400m receivables facility.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior reaction on the cash-flow line alone. Q2 2026 negative OCF coincided with -3.97%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The receivables composition (manufacturer rebates, about $347m) is in the 10-Q body, not the press release. If the market priced a working-capital trap, preview coverage would cite cash flow. None found does.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2 filings with the guidance finding, but this is a different line (cash, not EBITDA). The receivables facility funds a visible branded-GLP-1 ramp (Q3 revenue guide +47-50% y/y), so per the financing rule this is near zero, not a distress signal.

evidence.text: The Eucalyptus acquisition carries $683.9m of deferred payments in six quarterly instalments through 18 months after the June 2026 close, partly payable in Class A shares (capped at 19.9%). Of that, $537.4m is current, plus $163m of earn-outs, against $841m of cash and short-term investments and $1.365bn of convertible notes (Q2 10-Q). The Q3 call is the first update on how instalments are settled.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Buried in the 10-Q notes. If share settlement were in focus, the dilution would appear in previews. What the money buys is visible: international revenue of $131.4m in Q2 against a target of at least $600m for 2026. So the financing funds a ramp, and the size is small.
evidence.independence: Same 10-Q as the cash-flow finding, different line (acquisition consideration, not receivables).

evidence.text: Positioning is crowded into the print: short interest about 26-31% of float (31.5% on 2026-05-15, 58.7m shares and 4.5 days to cover on 2026-08-14), stock -23.8% over 20 days and about -7% on the print day with no stated cause, 25-delta skew -14.6 vol points (calls bid), put/call OI 0.32. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: High short interest has not stopped six of seven prints falling (baseline). The one up print, May 2025, was +18.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price: it lowers the bar rather than adding information. It is filed because the pre-print drawdown plus crowded short changes the asymmetry. If the option market saw a symmetric event, skew would not be -14.6.
evidence.independence: Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/hims/shortinterest) gives 61.2m shares, 3.2 days on 2026-07-10. The baseline skew and run-up are a separate source.

evidence.text: On 21 Oct HIMS launched injectable and oral testosterone replacement, its largest men's-health expansion. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock was flat on the launch day (closed unchanged at $29.21 on 2026-10-21).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock did not move on the launch. The first early-uptake number arrives on the call. It is small relative to revenue.

evidence.text: Hesai's reiterated FY2026 lidar shipment guide of 3.0-3.5m units (Q2 call, 2026-08-18) less H1 shipments of 1,099,998 (Q1 471,723 + Q2 628,275) and the Q3 guide of 800-850k implies Q4 shipments of 1.08-1.58m, i.e. +27% QoQ at the floor and ~+66% at the midpoint versus the Q3 top end; Benzinga's Q4 revenue consensus of US$237.5m (+44% QoQ vs Q3 consensus US$165.1m) bakes in that ramp, while China passenger retail fell 25% y/y in October (NEV retail -10%), Li Auto (the anchor multi-lidar customer) delivered 29,025 in October vs 31,767 a year earlier, and management on the Q2 call declined to comment on Xiaomi allocation after a competitor was added; a Q4 revenue guide or FY shipment range set below that ramp is the most likely negative this print carries.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 print (2026-11-11 is the analogue a year earlier, dated 2025-11-11): stock fell 5.03% intraday despite strong results and a raised FY guide because the Q4 outlook implied a slowdown (https://www.itiger.com/news/1183445981). Q2 2026 print (2026-08-18): -6.1% midday on a Q3 guide read as weak (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/hesai-sieht-q3-umsatz-bei-rmb-110115-mrd-aktie-fallt-nach-schwacherer-erwartung). The stock has sold the forward guide on both of the last two confirmed prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus for Q4 (US$237.5m) still carries the steep ramp the FY guide implies; if the market had priced a cut, that Q4 estimate would sit near the Q3 run-rate and skew would be put-bid rather than call-bid (-3.6). The 5-day +16% bounce into the print is not what a market positioned for a guide cut looks like. Against that: the stock is already -50% from its high, so part of a softer 2026 is in the level.
evidence.independence: China market: CPCA preliminary October 2026 data, passenger retail -25% y/y, NEV retail -10% (https://cnevpost.com/2026/11/04/china-oct-nev-retail-preliminary-cpca/). Customer: Li Auto October 2026 deliveries 29,025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001791706/000110465926120858/tm2628723d1_ex99-1.htm). Sector read: CATL's slower Q3 profit growth blamed on slower Chinese car sales hit Hesai -8% on 2026-10-21 (https://www.ibtimes.com.au/hesai-shares-fall-chinese-auto-sector-pressure-1877141). Macro-to-company transmission is a proxy; the company has not confirmed any Q4 softness.

evidence.text: Peers that reported Q3 2026 lidar volumes after Hesai last spoke printed very strong ADAS numbers: RoboSense Q3 total 595.6k units (+220.9% y/y, +53.1% QoQ) with ADAS 450.4k (+200.1% y/y), and Seyond Q3 268.9k (+217% y/y); Li Auto Q3 deliveries of 99,964 landed at the top of its 95-100k guide. Industry lidar demand in Q3 ran well above the car market, which makes Hesai's Q3 at or above the top of its 800-850k unit / RMB1.10-1.15bn guide more likely than not (Hesai's own Q3 needs only +27-35% QoQ vs RoboSense's +53%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hesai has not been paid for reported-quarter beats: Q3 2025 record results sold -5% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1183445981); Q4 2025 shipments 631k beat the 600k guide and 619k consensus with no reliable positive reaction found (https://longportapp.cn/topics/39486324). The reaction function damps this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Q3 consensus (~US$165.1m) sits at the guide midpoint and has not moved to reflect peers' October disclosures; if it had, consensus would be at or above the top of the range. Caveat in size: RoboSense's ADAS jump is partly share taken from Hesai (its Q3 ADAS 450k is close to Hesai's Q2 ADAS 485,904), so the read-across is net-positive industry volume but not clean.
evidence.independence: Seyond Q3 shipments 268.9k +217% y/y (https://www.bbtnews.com.cn/2026/1012/607643.shtml); Li Auto Q3 deliveries 99,964 at top of guide (https://cnevpost.com/2026/10/01/li-auto-sept-2026-deliveries/). Different issuers and documents from RoboSense.

evidence.text: Management said on the Q2 call that Q3 2026 is expected to be the quarter when non-ADAS lidar revenue is close to or above half of total revenue, that robotics and overseas lidar carry higher margins than domestic ADAS, and it kept the FY gross margin outlook at close to 40% after Q2's 40.1% (vs 42.5%) and operating income of only RMB2.2m (vs RMB22.9m); the mix shift gives Q3 gross margin a path to hold or tick up even as ADAS ASPs fall, with the SGI revenue guide already raised to RMB200-300m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin was the stated reason for the -5% on the Q3 2025 print (GM 42.1% vs 47.7%) (https://www.itiger.com/news/1183445981); a margin line that holds has not been tested as a positive.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side commentary since August has focused on falling lidar ASPs and price-for-volume (Dolphin Research, https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3946451052592521); a market that had priced the mix shift would not be treating margin as the bear case. Inside what the company guided (~40% FY GM), so sized small.
evidence.independence: Same document as finding 1 (Q2 call transcript), different line; Q2 6-K confirms GM 40.1% and lower ASPs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001861737/000110465926098050/tm2623467d1_ex99-1.htm).

evidence.text: The stock runs into the print up 16.3% in five sessions off a 52-week low of $11.85 (2026-10-22) with no company news found to explain the bounce, and this name has sold its last two confirmed prints (-5.03% Nov 2025, -5.3%/-6.1% Aug 2026); a pre-print rally on a sell-the-print name raises the bar for the release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: pre-market rally ahead of the print (+5.77% pre-market, https://www.itiger.com/news/1110421451) then -5.03% on the day (https://www.itiger.com/news/1183445981).
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up is in the sealed baseline (run_up_5d +16.26%), so this is mostly visible; what is not priced is the asymmetry it creates against the reaction function. Shrunk because short interest is 7.26 days to cover (squeeze mechanism) and calls are bid.
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_5d_pct 16.26); short interest from equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/hsai/shortinterest) cuts the other way.

With days to cover around 12.7, covering on any good launch number cannot happen in one session, which makes the upside tail asymmetric. The put skew suggests options traders price the downside tail more heavily, which is inconsistent with a crowded short the market has fully discounted.

evidence.text: Early payer policies are narrower than the FDA label. BCBS Michigan/BCN made Isembyld prior-authorization-required effective 2026-09-28/10-01 and covers only (a) patients diagnosed with later-onset Type 2/3 SMA, (b) patients not on invasive ventilation, (c) patients with no prior gene therapy, (d) prescriptions from a pediatric-neuromuscular neurologist, and (e) patients who have tried preferred drugs (step therapy). Approval lasts 6 months, and renewal requires a documented clinically significant motor response. The label covers everyone aged 2+ on an SMN2-targeted therapy. QualChoice (CP.PHAR.737) similarly excludes prior Zolgensma/Itvisma and requires a baseline HFMSE.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09-23 (PDF last modified; policy history effective 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-01)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior payer-access print. At approval the stock gave back its gains on pricing and the shift to execution (closed -6% on 2026-09-14).
evidence.why_not_priced: Payer medical policies are not aggregated by the wire or by previews. The street read the label as 'at the broad end of expectations'. If the market had absorbed plan-level criteria that exclude Type 1 survivors and adults outside pediatric-neuromuscular practices, and that require a 6-month response, the approval-day price-target raises would have come with access caveats. This is a proxy: two regional plans out of a market split about 50/50 commercial/government. The company's comments on the call on time-to-approval and access will show whether it generalises.
evidence.independence: Proxy. QualChoice criteria at https://www.qualchoice.com/media/9016/cpphar737_pepp.pdf and Blue Shield of California's PA-required policies (https://www.blueshieldca.com/content/dam/bsca/en/provider/docs/bsc-med-benefit-drug-policy/apitegromab-mstn-Isembyld-COMM-UMRx-provider.pdf) point the same way on PA friction. These are restrictions typical of a launch and are not company-confirmed.
